summary_html: Child achieves **permanency through legal guardianship** or kinship care. Federal programs provide funding parity with adoption for approved relatives.
authority_html:
- **Fostering Connections to Success and Increasing Adoptions Act (FCSIAA)** — kinship-guardianship assistance  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. § 673(d))** — authorizes Guardianship Assistance Program (GAP)

primary_citations.citation_text: Maryland - Md. Code, Family Law Article §§ 5-701 et seq. (Child Abuse and Neglect; definitions at § 5-701, mandatory reporting at §§ 5-704 and 5-705, investigation at § 5-706, appeal of findings at § 5-706.1)

provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Court held that a juvenile court abuses its discretion when it declines to terminate parental rights and instead leaves the child indefinitely in third-party custody after finding that neither parent can ever safely care for the child.
key_cases.relevance: It holds that indefinite third-party custody is not an acceptable substitute for permanency when reunification is impossible.
key_cases.quote: The finding that Father was not unfit is contradicted by the juvenile court's finding that reunification with either Father or Mother was not attainable within the foreseeable future

key_cases.citation: No. 1609, Sept. Term 2024 (Md. App. Ct. July 1, 2025)
key_cases.holding: The court held that in CINA cases a department is generally required under the ADA to make reasonable accommodations for parents with disabilities in providing reunification services, provided the parent makes the disability and needed accommodation known, and affirmed the award of custody and guardianship to the grandparents.
key_cases.relevance: It affirms custody and guardianship to relatives as the permanency outcome once reunification efforts are exhausted.
key_cases.quote: the Department is generally required under the ADA to make reasonable accommodations for parents with disabilities in rendering reunification efforts in CINA cases

key_cases.case_name: In re Adoption/Guardianship of Ta'Niya C.
key_cases.holding: Vacating a denial of termination, the Court clarified that Rashawn H. did not displace the best-interest standard: unfitness and exceptional circumstances are measured through, not apart from, the child's best interest, which remains the governing standard in TPR cases.
key_cases.relevance: Because guardianship alternatives are judged by the same best-interest inquiry, this case governs the choice between TPR and a permanent third-party arrangement.
key_cases.quote: we reexamine the law in this area and confirm once again that the child's best interest is the prevailing standard in these determinations

key_cases.holding: The Court reversed a grandparent-visitation order and overruled contrary prior decisions, holding that Maryland's grandparent visitation statute may be applied constitutionally only after a threshold finding of parental unfitness or exceptional circumstances showing current or future detriment to the child from the absence of visitation, before any best-interest analysis.
key_cases.relevance: It fixes the constitutional predicate a kinship caregiver must satisfy before a court may order a third-party access arrangement as part of permanency.
key_cases.quote: there must be a finding of either parental unfitness or exceptional circumstances demonstrating the current or future detriment to the child, absent visitation from his or her grandparents

key_cases.holding: The Court reversed an award of custody to maternal grandparents, holding that in a private custody dispute between a fit natural parent and third parties the court may not reach the best-interest test unless it first finds both parents unfit or extraordinary circumstances significantly detrimental to the child's remaining in parental custody.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Maryland decision establishing the parental presumption that governs any third-party custody or guardianship permanency arrangement, and the authority Ta'Niya C. and Victoria C. are reconciling.
key_cases.quote: in private custody actions involving private third-parties where the parents are fit, absent extraordinary (i.e., exceptional) circumstances, the constitutional right is the ultimate determinative factor

extended_foster_care_age: Up to the 21st birthday, and only while the young person meets one of five conditions: completing secondary education or a program leading to an equivalent credential; enrolled in an institution providing post-secondary or vocational education; participating in a program or activity designed to promote or remove barriers to employment; employed at least 80 hours per month; or incapable of any of those due to a medical condition documented in the case plan (COMAR 07.02.11.04B). Not eligible for out-of-home placement if married, in the military, or not complying with those conditions (COMAR 07.02.11.04C). Re-entry: the juvenile court has jurisdiction over a former CINA whose commitment to the local department was rescinded after age 18 but before age 20 years 6 months and who did not exit foster care due to reunification, adoption, guardianship, marriage, or uniformed services duty, and that jurisdiction continues until age 21 (Md. Code, Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 3-804(b)(2) and (c)).

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
